Etymology: [一] A single horizontal stroke — a direct pictograph of one tally mark.
[二] Two horizontal strokes stacked — a direct pictograph of two tally marks.
[三] Three horizontal strokes stacked — a direct pictograph of three tally marks.
[囗] (enclosure) + 儿 (legs) — originally a pictograph of a divided space, standardised over centuries into the current form.
[一] (top stroke) + 乂 (crossed strokes) + 一 (bottom stroke) — originated as a crossed tally mark between two lines in ancient script.
[八] (diverging strokes, below) + 亠 (top dot and stroke) — the lower 八 component represents splitting; the shape was repurposed phonetically for six.
[一] (horizontal stroke) + a vertical hook below — originated as a pictograph of a cut or notch, borrowed phonetically for the number seven.
[八] Two diverging strokes — a pictograph of something splitting apart, borrowed for the number eight.
[乙] A curving stroke with a hook — originated as a pictograph of a bent arm, borrowed phonetically for the number nine.
[十] A vertical and horizontal stroke crossing — originally a single vertical line with a central mark indicating a complete count.
[白] (white, below) + 一 (one, top stroke) — one above white; thought to derive from a pictograph of a thumb representing a large counting unit.
[十] (ten, lower strokes) + 一 (one, top stroke) — a person with a mark above indicating a great multitude.
[一] (top stroke) — originally a pictograph of a scorpion in oracle bone script, associated with swarming abundance; borrowed for ten thousand.
[冂] (enclosure frame) + 人 (person, inside) — simplified from 圓, a round enclosure; the circular shape gave rise to the meaning of circle and currency.
[日] A circle with a central stroke — direct pictograph of the sun with a sunspot, distinguishing it from the moon 月.
[月] A crescent shape — direct pictograph of the crescent moon; used for month because months were tracked by lunar cycles.
[火] A central upward flame stroke with two outer strokes — direct pictograph of a flame with sparks flying to each side.
[水] A central vertical stream with strokes on each side — direct pictograph of flowing water with splashing tributaries.
[木] A vertical trunk with branches above and roots below — direct pictograph of a tree, with the horizontal stroke as the ground line.
[金] 人 (person, top) + 土 (earth, below) + two dots — pictograph of gold nuggets buried in the earth beneath a covering mound.
[土] A horizontal stroke on the ground with a vertical stem rising from it — pictograph of a mound or clod of earth.
[干] (stem, upper) + 人 (person, lower) — originally depicted a person carrying a bundle of grain, representing the annual harvest cycle.
[日] (sun) + 寺 (temple) — the sun's position over a temple marking the hours; temples historically rang bells to mark the time.
[刀] (knife, below) + 八 (diverging, top) — a knife dividing something into parts; to separate or divide.
[十] (vertical stroke below) + 八 (diverging, top) — something split apart down the middle; half.
[人] (person, top) + 口 (mouth, below) — a person with something at their mouth; the breath or utterance of this very moment.
[儿] (legs, below) + 之 (going forward, top) — legs moving forward; to go ahead or precede.
[母] (mother) with a modified top — derived from mother 母; the sense of recurring nourishment extended to mean every or each time.
[辶] (movement/road, outer) + 周 (circuit/cycle, inner) — movement through a full cycle; one complete circuit of seven days.
[日] (sun) + 翟 (pheasant/brightness) — the brilliance of a celestial body; used to denote the luminaries (sun, moon, five planets) assigned to days of the week.
[十] (crossing stroke) — originally a pictograph of a pestle; noon was the midpoint of the day's cycle, one of the twelve Earthly Branches.
[刀] (knife, lower right) + 止 (foot, upper left) + 舟 (boat) — a foot moving forward with a cutting motion; to advance or go before.
[彳] (step, left) + 幺 (small) + 夂 (trailing foot) — a foot trailing behind small steps; to follow after or be behind.
[月] (moon, right) + 十 + 日 (sun, left components) — the moon still visible as the sun rises; the moment of early morning.
[日] (sun, bottom) + 尺 (measure/length) — the sun at its measured height overhead; the middle of the day.
[夕] (evening, outer) + 亦 (a person with armpits marked) — a person sheltering under the dark of evening; night.
[夕] A crescent shape — a simplified pictograph of the crescent moon appearing at dusk, representing evening.
[大] (a person with outstretched arms, below) + 一 (a stroke above the head) — the great expanse above a person's head; heaven or sky.
[气] (steam/breath, outer) + 米 (rice, inner) — steam rising from cooking rice; the vital breath or energy that sustains life.
[雨] A horizontal top stroke (sky) with four dots below (raindrops) — direct pictograph of rain falling from a cloud.
[雨] (rain, top) + 彗 (broom, lower) — rain that must be swept away; snow.
[虫] (insect, inner) + 冂 (enclosure/sail frame, outer) — insects carried on the breeze inside an enclosing current of air; wind.
[穴] (cave/hole, top) + 工 (work/hollow out, bottom) — a hollowed-out cave opening upward into the vast emptiness; sky or empty space.
[山] Three peaks rising from a base — direct pictograph of a mountain range with a taller central peak flanked by two smaller ones.
[川] Three vertical flowing lines — direct pictograph of water flowing downward in a river.
[田] A rectangle divided into four plots by a cross — direct pictograph of a rice paddy divided into sections by paths or dikes.
[木] (tree) × 3 — three trees together form a dense forest; a logical compound of tree repeated.
[木] (tree) × 2 — two trees side by side form a grove or small woods.
[艸] (grass/plant, top) + 化 (change/transform, bottom) — a plant in transformation; the blooming flower.
[艸] (plant, top) + 早 (early, bottom) — early-sprouting plants; grass.
[石] 厂 (cliff, top) + 口 (mouth/block, bottom) — a block fallen from a cliff face; a stone or rock.
[虫] Originally a pictograph of a coiled snake; later generalised to cover all small crawling creatures including insects.
[大] (large/person with arms out) + a dot — a person-like figure with a distinguishing mark; the dot differentiates dog from the character for large 大.
[魚] A pictograph showing a fish head at top, scales in the body, and a tail fin at the bottom — direct pictograph of a fish.
[鳥] A pictograph of a bird with a head, body, wing, and tail — direct pictograph of a bird, distinguished from 隹 (short-tailed bird) by the long tail strokes.
[米] A central stroke with grains radiating outward — pictograph of rice grains scattered around a central stem.
[牛] A pictograph of a cow's horns and head viewed from the front — direct pictograph of a cow's face.
[馬] A pictograph of a horse showing head, mane, body, and four legs — direct pictograph of a horse.
[王] (king, the same strokes) + a dot — three horizontal strokes connected by a vertical (strung jewels), with a dot added to distinguish jewel from king 王.
[王] Three horizontal strokes connected by a vertical — representing heaven, earth, and humanity united by the ruler who stands between them.
[門] A direct pictograph of two swinging gate doors with a horizontal bar across the top — a symmetrical double-doored gate.
[車] A pictograph of a wheeled cart viewed from above — a central axle with two wheels on either side and a body in the middle.
[雨] (rain, top) + 申 (lightning bolt, bottom) — lightning flashing from a rain cloud; electricity.
[辶] (movement along a path, outer) + 首 (head, inner) — a head leading the way along a path; road or way.
[馬] (horse, left) + 尺 (measure, right) — a measured stopping point for horses on a post road; a station.
[广] (building/lean-to, top) + 占 (to occupy, bottom) — a building that occupies a place for trade; a shop.
[囗] (enclosure/border, outer) + 玉 (jewel/land, inner) — a precious territory enclosed within borders; a country.
[田] (rice field, left) + 丁 (a nail/block, right) — a marked-out field settlement; a town or district block.
[木] (tree, left) + 寸 (a small measure, right) — trees measured out for settlement; a small clustered community.
[亠] (top) + 口 (mouth) + 小 (small legs below) — a pictograph of a tall building or watchtower on a hill, representing an elevated capital city.
[木] (wood/structure, left) + 交 (intersect/exchange, right) — a wooden structure where learning is exchanged; a school.
[示] (altar/spirit, left) + 土 (earth, right) — an earth altar for worship; extended to mean a gathered institution or company.
[人] (people, top) + 云 (gathering clouds/speaking, bottom) — people coming together to speak; to meet or assemble.
[宀] (roof, top) + 豕 (pig, bottom) — a roof sheltering a pig; in ancient times keeping a pig under the roof indicated a settled household.
[宀] (roof, top) + 至 (to arrive, bottom) — the place one arrives at under a roof; an interior room.
[見] (see, right) + 立 (stand) + 木 (tree, left components) — a figure standing in a tree watching over; a parent keeping watch.
[父] A pictograph of a hand gripping a rod or tool — the hand that wields authority and works; father.
[母] A pictograph of a kneeling woman with two dots marking the breasts — the nursing figure; mother.
[儿] (legs/person, bottom) + 口 (mouth, top) — a person who speaks first or speaks above; the elder who leads with words.
[女] (woman, left) + 市 (market/gather, right) — a woman of the marketplace or gathering; the older sister who manages affairs.
[弓] (bow, outer strokes) + 丨 (vertical) — a pictograph of a cord wound around a stake; the younger one who follows in order.
[女] (woman, left) + 未 (not yet/young tree, right) — a woman who is not yet fully grown; younger sister.
[子] A pictograph of a swaddled infant with arms outstretched — direct pictograph of a baby or young child.
[人] Two strokes — a direct pictograph of a person standing upright seen from the side, one stroke the body and one the leg.
[女] A pictograph of a kneeling or seated figure with crossed arms — a direct pictograph of a woman in a traditional seated posture.
[田] (rice field, top) + [力] (strength/muscle, bottom) — strength applied in the field; the man who works the land.
[又] (right hand) × 2 — two right hands clasped together; friendship expressed through a handshake.
[夕] (evening, top) + 口 (mouth, bottom) — calling out one's name with one's mouth in the dark of evening when faces cannot be seen.
[生] A sprouting plant growing from the ground — direct pictograph of a plant pushing up through the earth; life and birth.
[子] (child, bottom) + 冖 (cover) + 爻 (interaction, top) — a child under a roof receiving instruction; to study or learn.
[文] A pictograph of a person with a mark or tattoo on the chest — the original meaning was a pattern or marking; extended to writing and text.
[宀] (roof, top) + 子 (child, bottom) — a child under a roof being taught; a written character learned in a place of instruction.
[言] (speech, left) + 吾 (I/my, right) — my own speech; a language or the way one speaks.
[言] (speech, left) + 舌 (tongue, right) — the tongue making speech; to talk or tell a story.
[言] (speech, left) + 売 (sell/exchange, right) — exchanging meaning through speech marks; to read.
[曰] (say/sun, bottom) + 筆 (brush strokes, top) — a brush making marks to say something; to write.
[耳] (ear, inner) + 門 (gate, outer) — an ear at the gate listening; to hear or ask.
[目] (eye, top) + 儿 (person/legs, bottom) — a person with an eye prominent; to see or look.
[行] A pictograph of a crossroads — left and right strokes representing a junction of paths; to go or travel.
[木] (tree) + 人 (people on either side) — originally a pictograph of a wheat plant; borrowed phonetically for to come, as wheat came from the west.
[巾] (cloth, lower right) + 帚 (broom, right) + 刀 (knife left components) — a broom sweeping the way back home; to return.
[入] Two strokes converging downward — a pictograph of something pushing inward or entering through an opening.
[凵] (open container, bottom) + 山 (rising shape, top) — something rising up and out of a container; to exit or leave.
[人] (person, left) + 木 (tree, right) — a person leaning against a tree in the shade; to rest.
[立] A pictograph of a person standing upright on a horizontal ground line — direct pictograph of a figure standing.
[人] (person, left) + 吏 (official, right) — a person directing an official; to employ or use.
[矢] (arrow, left) + 口 (mouth, right) — words as swift and sure as an arrow; to know with certainty.
[心] (heart, bottom) + 田 (field/brain-like grid, top) — the heart working through something methodically; to think.
[手] (hand, left) + 寺 (temple/maintain, right) — a hand that maintains or keeps steady; to hold.
[羊] (sheep/wool, top) + 目 (eye) + 人 (person below) — a person layered with wool seen clearly; to wear or to arrive (reach one's destination).
[士] (samurai/person, top) + 買 (buy, simplified below) — simplified from 賣; a person exchanging goods; to sell.
[貝] (shell/money, bottom) + 网 (net, top) — netting valuables or money; to buy.
[貝] (shell/money, bottom) + 代 (substitute/replace, top) — money given temporarily in place of something else; to lend.
[人] (person, left) + 昔 (long ago, right) — a person taking something from the past that must be returned; to borrow.
[人] (person, left) + 主 (master/lord, right) — a person who is master of a place; to dwell or reside.
[食] Originally a pictograph of a covered vessel of rice on a stand — the complete meal setting; to eat.
[食] (eating vessel, left) + 欠 (open mouth/yawning, right) — an open mouth tilted toward a food vessel; to drink.
[木] (tree, lower) + 人 with legs astride (top) — a person mounted atop a tree or post; to ride or board.
[阜] (mound/steps, left) + 夅 (descending feet, right) — feet descending a mound or steps; to get off or come down.
[刀] (knife, right) + 七 (seven, left — used phonetically) — a knife in action; to cut.
[門] (gate, outer) + 开 (two hands lifting a bar, inner) — two hands lifting the crossbar of a gate; to open.
[又] (hand, right) + 耳 (ear, left) — a hand grasping an ear, from the ancient practice of taking a defeated enemy's ear as proof of victory; to take.
